data.narrative:
Quantum Motion is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $160M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers across the sector—3 publicly listed (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Systems) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, and Infleqtion—though meaningful same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within quantum computing remain sparse.

Stage-progression analysis, the sole applicable method here, uses the $160M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding an implied value of $272M. This reflects incremental progression risk appropriate to the stage and sector maturity. Peer-median analysis is not applicable; while six quantum computing peers exist, none cluster tightly enough around Quantum Motion's current stage and valuation tier to satisfy minimum comparability thresholds (≥3 datapoints required). Drawing on the full-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise given the wide dispersion in quantum computing valuations.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $231M (low) to $313M (high), centered at $272M. This range reflects single-method triangulation and carries material uncertainty. Key variables affecting any revision include: (1) technology differentiation relative to the peer set, particularly around scalability and qubit fidelity; (2) commercial traction and IP strength, which are not quantified here; and (3) momentum in the broader quantum sector, currently reflected in public comps but volatile. Additional data on revenue, customer concentration, or technical milestones would narrow this band materially.
